Name: Falco rule: Contact K8S API Server From Container
Synopsis: A container process made a direct network connection to the Kubernetes API server, which is unusual for most workloads and can indicate an attempt at cluster-wide privilege escalation.
Solution: Restrict the workload's service account permissions and network policy so it cannot reach the API server unless genuinely required.

Name: Falco rule: Read sensitive file trusted after startup
Synopsis: A normally-trusted process read a sensitive file well after container startup, outside its expected initialization window.
Solution: Confirm this matches expected application behavior; if not, investigate for possible compromise of the trusted process.

Name: Falco rule: Read sensitive file untrusted
Synopsis: A process not on the expected allowlist read a sensitive file (e.g. /etc/shadow) inside the container.
Solution: Verify whether the reading process is legitimate; restrict file permissions and container user privileges to least privilege.

Name: Falco rule: Netcat Remote Code Execution in Container
Synopsis: The netcat utility was executed inside a container in a mode consistent with establishing a reverse or bind shell.
Solution: Investigate the container immediately for signs of remote command execution; remove netcat from production container images.

Name: Falco rule: PTRACE attached to process
Synopsis: A process used ptrace to attach to another running process, a technique that can be used for legitimate debugging or for credential/memory inspection by an attacker.
Solution: Verify the attaching process is an authorized debugging tool; restrict the SYS_PTRACE capability for workloads that don't need it.

Name: Falco rule: Disallowed SSH Connection Non Standard Port
